arguments.sql: SELECT SUM(t.amount_usd_cents) / 100.0 AS total_net_usd, SUM(CASE WHEN t.amount_usd_cents > 0 THEN t.amount_usd_cents ELSE 0 END) / 100.0 AS total_positive_only_usd, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions t JOIN cards c ON c.id = t.card_id WHERE c.credit_limit_usd_cents > 2000000
arguments.explanation: Shows the total dollar amount of all transactions on cards with a credit limit above $20,000. It gives two totals, one with every amount and one with positive amounts only, plus the number of transactions.
assumptions: "Above $20,000" means a credit limit strictly greater than $20,000 (2,000,000 cents).
The meaning of negative amounts isn't documented, so I didn't assume they are refunds. The first total includes them and the second leaves them out.
All transactions from 2019-01-01 to 2019-10-31 count, whatever their error status.
